knowledge:
- key_parameters: np=The number of random gene pairs to sample (e.g., 1000) ;; seed=The random seed for reproducible sampling ;; scatter=Logical indicating whether to plot individual pair correlations as a scatter plot ;; curve=Logical indicating whether to plot the average correlation curve ;; model=Logical indicating whether to overlay a simple theoretical model curve for lack of normalization ;; cond=A character vector or list of factors defining panel labels for comparing multiple datasets or expression measures ;; groups=A vector or list of vectors defining gene pair groups to overlay multiple correlation curves in the same plot ;; auto.key=Logical indicating whether to automatically draw a legend for grouped plots ;; nint=Number of intervals for computing average correlations ;; ylim=Limits for the vertical axis of the plot
- alternatives: None mentioned; the package is designed to compare different low-level processing methods (such as MAS5 vs. RMA) on the same dataset.
- when_to_use: Use when analyzing high-density oligonucleotide/one-dye microarray chips (e.g., Affymetrix HGU133A) to check if low-variance genes suffer from systematic normalization artifacts.
- pitfalls: Not extensively tested on cDNA/two-dye chips ;; Not suitable for small or boutique chips where the assumption of zero average correlation between random gene pairs does not hold ;; Does not measure other aspects of expression measure quality, such as bias or fold-change estimation accuracy.

workflows.name: microarray_normalization_diagnostic
workflows.intent: Diagnose microarray normalization quality by plotting correlation against variability for random gene pairs, with options to compare different normalization methods and gene groups.
workflows.stages: 1. Sample random pairs of genes using CorrSample ;; 2. Generate diagnostic plots of correlation vs. standard deviation using plot ;; 3. Compare multiple normalization methods or datasets by passing multiple CorrSample objects to plot ;; 4. Group gene pairs by external metadata (e.g., present/absent calls) and overlay grouped curves using the groups argument
workflows.code:
corrA.rma = CorrSample(datA.rma, np=1000, seed=213)
plot(corrA.rma)
corrA.rma[1:5,]
jj = plot(corrA.rma)
print(jj)
jj = plot(corrA.rma, scatter=TRUE, curve=TRUE)
print(jj)
corrA.mas5 = CorrSample(datA.mas5, np=1000, seed=213)
plot(corrA.mas5, corrA.rma, cond=c("MAS5","RMA"))
corrB.rma = CorrSample(datB.rma, np=1000, seed=214)
corrB.mas5 = CorrSample(datB.mas5, np=1000, seed=214)
plot(corrA.mas5, corrA.rma, corrB.mas5, corrB.rma, cond=c("MAS5/A","RMA/A","MAS5/B","RMA/B"))
plot(corrA.mas5, corrA.rma, corrB.mas5, corrB.rma, cond=list(c("MAS5","RMA","MAS5","RMA"), c("A","A","B","B")))
jj = plot(corrA.mas5, corrA.rma, cond=c("MAS5","RMA"))
print(jj)
jj = plot(corrA.mas5, corrA.rma, corrB.mas5, corrB.rma, cond=list(c("MAS5","RMA","MAS5","RMA"), c("A","A","B","B")))
print(jj)
pcntA = rowSums(datA.amp=="P")
pcntA.pairs = (pcntA[corrA.rma$ndx1]+pcntA[corrA.rma$ndx2])/2
pgrpA.pairs = cut(pcntA.pairs, c(0, 10, 20, 30), include.lowest=TRUE)
table(pgrpA.pairs)
plot(corrA.rma, groups=pgrpA.pairs, auto.key=TRUE)
jj = plot(corrA.rma, groups=pgrpA.pairs, auto.key=TRUE)
print(jj)
jj = plot(corrA.mas5, corrA.rma, cond=c("MAS5","RMA"), groups=list(pgrpA.pairs, pgrpA.pairs), nint=5, ylim=c(-0.25, 0.4))
print(jj)
